title: Supplier integration pathways and legal exec brief
summary: Intro to vendor onboarding path, high-level legal and security asks for PHI/HIPAA, confirmation of DPA/MSA redline process, pricing cadence for committed capacity and pilot, and schedulings for deep-security review.
topics: MSA / DPA redline and approval path
Pricing for hosted vs dedicated and committed discounts
Data residency, KMS/HSM integration, HIPAA considerations
Next steps: share redlines, schedule security deep dive, procurement timeline

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Asha, Marco, Priya (Redwood); Olivia, Raj, Lena, Tom (Novus)
Shared artifacts: Redwood DPA draft (link), Pricing worksheet (link), VPC diagram (to be shared)

[00:00] Asha (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we know holiday season's busy so we'll try to keep this tight. I'm Asha, AE for Novus. Marco and Priya from my side. Can folks introduce quickly?
[00:18] Olivia (Novus): Hi Olivia, procurement. We'll be focusing on contracting and timing.
[00:24] Raj (Novus): Raj, security. I'll ask the deep technical questions, HIPAA and KMS primarily.
[00:28] Lena (Novus): Lena, counsel. I'll look at indemnity, DPA language and data residency.
[00:32] Tom (Novus): Tom, IT ops, operational constraints and network egress.
[00:36] Marco (Redwood): Hi all, Marco, solutions engineer. I'll walk through deployment options and the KMS bits.

[01:02] Asha: Quick agenda: 1) contracting path (MSA + DPA), 2) security asks, 3) pricing/po path for pilot, 4) timelines. Any additions?
[01:09] Olivia: That covers it. We also need to confirm whether you support private deployments in our VPC and if you can sign a HIPAA BA or at least a DPA with PHI clauses.

[02:05] Marco: Short answer — we support three modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem). For PHI we recommend dedicated or private. Hosted can be used with strict controls but it depends on your risk appetite.
[02:22] Raj: When you say private — is that customer-managed VPC peering or a fully on-prem appliance? We need to know KMS integration, HSM compatibility.
[02:36] Marco: We offer both. VPC peering with a private control plane is the typical path; we also have an on-prem package for air-gapped scenarios. KMS integrations include AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and we support external HSM via standard APIs. There's a diagram we'll share.

[04:12] Lena: On the DPA/MSA front, our counsel will likely push back on data processing definitions, subprocessor lists, and liability caps for PHI. What's Redwood's baseline?
[04:28] Asha: Our standard MSA has a commercial liability cap tied to fees, and the DPA includes subprocessors and SOC 2 attestation. For PHI we can add clarifying language and sign BA attachments but we'll need to scope whether Redwood is a BA or a processor depending on use.
[04:49] Lena: We'll need the actual MSA and DPA to review; can you circulate annotated copies?
[04:55] Asha: Absolutely — we'll send our current DPA and a suggested minimal redline for the MSA after this call.

[06:00] Tom: Network egress — if we run in dedicated mode, are there fixed egress fees? Our finance team flags variable cloud egress as a blocker.
[06:12] Marco: For dedicated pools, we provide a predictable pricing plan with capped egress buckets per commit. If you need a fully private on-prem model, egress isn't applicable. We'll include egress scenarios in the pricing worksheet.

[07:05] Olivia: Speaking of pricing, what's the pilot pricing? We usually ask for a short POC with limited spend before committing.
[07:18] Priya: For pilots we typically do a 30-day pilot with a defined token cap and a not-to-exceed cost. We can offer pilot rates and apply credit toward committed capacity if you convert. We'll send a pilot SOW and a pricing sheet.

[08:10] Raj: For security posture, we need SOC 2 Type II reports, pen test summaries, and a list of subprocessors. Also, what about logging/audit retention? We need long-term audit logs for compliance.
[08:26] Marco: We have SOC 2 Type II; pen test summaries are available under NDA. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM — retention configurable per contract. The console shows token-level usage and traces.

[09:40] Lena: Indemnity and PI exposure — our legal will be looking at liability carve-outs for PHI. Is Redwood open to negotiation on liability cap for PHI-related breaches?
[09:53] Asha: We can discuss higher caps for PHI where contractual commitments and controls are in place; obviously we need to balance risk with insurance and technical controls. We'll outline options in the redline.

[11:05] Olivia: Timeline: procurement wants a PO by end of December if legal signs off quickly. Is that feasible?
[11:17] Asha: Tight but possible. If we get MSA redlines this week and security signoff next week, we can aim for a pilot kickoff mid-December and PO before year-end.

[12:40] Marco: Technical note on latency and SLA — hosted endpoints have a typical p50 token latency of 40-80ms in our benchmarks; dedicated pools can guarantee lower tail latencies and throughput. For mission-critical workflows we recommend dedicated capacity with canary fallbacks.
[12:58] Raj: What does your SLA specifically cover? Uptime, latency SLOs, and remedies?
[13:07] Asha: Our standard SLA is 99.9% for hosted API for enterprise customers with credits for sustained downtime. For dedicated customers we can negotiate tighter SLOs with service credits or remediation and runbooks. We'll share the SLA appendix.

[14:50] Lena: On data residency: some of our systems live in EU; is there an option to pin data to a region? We need data residency guarantees in the DPA.
[15:03] Marco: Yes, request-based routing can pin workloads to specific regions. For Private deployments, you control physical location. We'll include region-residency clauses.

[16:30] Tom: For SSO — we need SAML/SCIM provisioning and RBAC integration. How mature are your SSO flows?
[16:40] Priya: SAML and OIDC supported, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC in the console. We can work with your IdP team in the pilot phase to do a test integration.

[18:02] Raj: KMS flow question — if customer-provided KMS, do you store plaintext keys? How is encryption at rest handled?
[18:14] Marco: We never store plaintext keys. We use envelope encryption; customer KMS controls root key, and we manage ephemeral keys for tokenization. We'll include a KMS flow diagram showing HSM integrations.

[20:00] Asha: Quick check — competitors. Are you evaluating other vendors?
[20:06] Olivia: We looked at Anthropic and a couple of open-source stack vendors that do self-host. Price and control are main factors.
[20:13] Asha: Noted. We sometimes align on a pilot to show latency/cost delta vs other stacks.

[22:30] Lena: A couple of burning legal points — subprocessor list granularity and data deletion obligations. We need clear SLA for deletion of ephemeral caches and a clause about forensic access for audits.
[22:45] Marco: We can commit to deletion timelines, and we have audit hooks for forensic exports under NDA. We'll propose explicit deletion windows in the DPA.

[25:10] Olivia: Finance asks about billing cadence — monthly net 30 or annual prepay? We have a preference for PO/annual commitments for discounting.
[25:24] Asha: We offer monthly and annual committer options; committed annual gives unit discounts and reserved capacity. We can support PO and invoicing terms. We'll align on acceptable billing path for Novus.

[27:50] Tom: Do you have a data transfer fee schedule for EU <-> US cross-border traffic? That affects our cost model if we keep logs centralized.
[28:05] Marco: Cross-region transfer fees are outlined in the pricing worksheet; we can also propose routing to minimize cross-border egress. For heavy cross-region logs we can propose log replication options with separate pricing.

[30:00] Priya: Next steps recap — Redwood will: 1) send DPA + MSA baseline, 2) share pricing worksheet and pilot SOW, 3) Marco will create KMS/VPC diagram, 4) schedule security deep dive.
[30:18] Olivia: Correct. Also procurement will share PO template and internal approvers.

[31:40] Lena: Asha, on indemnity and liability caps — can you send examples of insurance coverage or cyber E&O limits? We may need that for our risk committee.
[31:51] Asha: Yes, we can share summary of our insurance coverage and typical limits; full certificates available under NDA.

[34:00] Raj: For the security deep dive I'd like to involve our cloud infra folks and a lead architect. Can we do a scheduled 60–90 minute session next week?
[34:12] Marco: Absolutely. We suggest focusing on KMS, network topology, and logging during that session.

[36:30] Olivia: If legal flags something big, will that delay PO? We need to understand gating items now.
[36:40] Lena: Biggest gates for us: DPA assurances on PHI, indemnity, and subprocessors. If Redwood can accept narrow redlines and provide SOC 2, we can expedite.

[38:00] Asha: We'll aim to keep redlines minimal and propose specific language for PHI carve-outs. We'll follow up with a proposed DPA with deletion and residency language for review.

[40:20] Marco: Logistics: I'll send a VPC peering checklist and a sample network ACL configuration. That should help Tom estimate on-prem bandwidth and firewall changes.
[40:35] Tom: Great, that speeds internal scoping.

[42:50] Priya: Pricing note — for an annual commit we can offer a tiered discount starting at 15% depending on commit size; we'll put numbers in the pricing sheet. Pilot credit can be applied to first invoice.

[44:10] Olivia: Sounds good. If we get your docs by Friday and legal returns comments early next week, procurement can aim for PO by 12/22.
[44:25] Asha: We'll prioritize.

[45:30] Lena: Last quick question — do you provide a mutual audit clause or is it Redwood-side only? Sometimes we push for auditor access.
[45:41] Marco: We can accommodate auditor access under standard procedures and NDA; we'll show typical language.

[46:50] Asha: Ok team, thanks — we'll send the MSA/DPA + pricing + KMS diagram. I'll follow up with a calendar invite for security deep dive. Anything else?
[46:58] Olivia: None from procurement.
[47:03] Raj: All good.
[47:10] Lena: Thanks, talk soon.
[47:22] Asha: Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
